name: Misogyny
summary: The reference and scholarly works that define misogyny describe it as hatred of, aversion to, or prejudice against women, or (in Kate Manne's account) as the attempt to police and punish women who challenge male dominance. They describe an attitude and a way of enforcing patriarchy; none sets out a programme or positions on laws, institutions or policy.
scope: The attitude named by the term, as the dictionaries (Merriam-Webster, Dictionary.com, Cambridge), Britannica and Manne's scholarship define it. Excludes the texts of individual misogynous writers and of patriarchal regimes, religions or movements, which would be coatracks unless these sources tie them to the term, and feminist or critic accounts of what misogynists believe.
